details: Houthi attacks have led to the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and halted oil loadings at Yanbu. This disruption pushed WTI crude prices to $103.60 and the 10-year Treasury yield to 5%, raising inflation concerns and causing Bitcoin to decline by approximately 4% in 24 hours. This event highlights how geopolitical tensions can directly impact energy markets and subsequently influence cryptocurrency valuations by increasing risk aversion among investors.
title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Oil Drive WTI to $103, Bitcoin Falls

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve has increased interest rates by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75-4.00%, marking the first hike in over three years. This decision, aimed at combating persistently high inflation, which has been fueled by soaring fuel prices amidst the US-Iran war, comes despite President Trump's preference for lower rates. This monetary tightening typically reduces liquidity in financial markets, making riskier assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive.
title: US Fed Raises Interest Rates First Time in Three Years Amid Inflation

details: The US House of Representatives has passed a bill providing President Trump with expanded authority to sanction Russia and its enablers. This bipartisan legislation aims to further cut off funding for Russia's war in Ukraine, though some lawmakers expressed concern about potential misuse of presidential power. Increased sanctions and ongoing geopolitical friction can create broader market uncertainty, which often leads to a risk-off sentiment that can negatively affect cryptocurrency markets.
title: US Lawmakers Pass Bill Granting Trump More Power to Sanction Russia
